correctness.rationale: Every palindromic run symbol sequence has an odd number of runs, and a subsequence has no more runs than its parent. For words with <=2k+1 runs, a palindrome with <=2k-1 runs is specified by <=k initial symbol/length choices and contributes only E(w)<=q sum_{j<k}(q-1)^j n^{j+1}=O_{q,k}(n^k). A 2k+1-run palindrome must select every parent run; it exists only for a 2k+1-run palindromic skeleton and has exactly L(w)=r_{k+1} product_{i<=k} min(r_i,r_{2k+2-i}) distinct strings. Set t_i=min(...) and c=r_center; 2 sum t_i+c<=n. AM–GM bounds L<=n^{k+1}/[2^k(k+1)^{k+1}]. Alternating two-symbol palindrome skeleton with each flank length floor(n/[2(k+1)]) and center length n-2k floor(...) attains the leading term. The equality-case stability follows from compactness and AM–GM uniqueness; the n-2sum t_i-c deficit is the sum of absolute differences in mirrored run lengths. This proves the iff rigidity with fixed q,k and excludes a mere finite extrapolation. Fresh dynamic enumeration directly counted distinct PALINDROME STRINGS in 21,690 word/k instances, confirming top-run formula.

originality.rationale: Mahalingam–Pandoh (2021) study distinct scattered palindromes but optimize by different-letter count and general Fibonacci-type bounds; a fixed run-budget leading coefficient and run-length rigidity were not found in its inspected theorems. Liron–Langberg (2012) give extremal counts for arbitrary fixed-length deletion subsequences, which ignore palindromicity. Resultary related sequence coding results do not imply this all-length palindrome count. The sharp leading coefficient and stability under a natural run constraint are qualified original.
residual_risks: An older run-bounded palindrome count under another terminology could give the same polynomial coefficient.
Asymptotic rigidity is fixed q and k; it neither proves exact maximum for every n nor handles increasing k.
